page: Microsoft Azure D16pds_v7 belongs to the general purpose Dpdsv7 instance family and is built upon an arm64 processor architecture running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a uniform allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. This hardware configuration does not feature GPU accelerators, directing all computational processing through the ARM execution pipeline.

The instance includes 945 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, offering dedicated scratch disk space for high-throughput input and output operations directly attached to the host. The D16pds_v7 does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring virtual network routing or allocated public addressing for external network reachability. Premium storage capabilities are supported, allowing integration with external managed storage alongside the local high-speed disk.

The ARM instruction set combined with a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio provides an efficient compute profile for modern cloud environments, delivering competitive resource density compared to traditional x86 alternatives. A primary technical tradeoff involves software compatibility, as binaries and dependencies must compile natively for arm64 without reliance on legacy x86 vector extensions like AVX. Given its balanced resources and substantial fast local storage, the D16pds_v7 is suited for web serving, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, relational databases, caching layers, and intermediate data processing jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure D16pds_v7 is an ARM-based general purpose virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance includes 16 dedicated ARM64 vCPUs alongside 64.0 GB of memory, delivering a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture features 945 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD disk space, enabling fast I/O throughput for applications requiring direct low-latency disk operations. There are no dedicated hardware graphics processing units or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with this configuration. Because of its ARM architecture and balanced resource footprint, the instance offers strong cost efficiency across multi-threaded applications capable of running on arm64 instruction sets. Workloads well matched to the D16pds_v7 include microservices architectures, web application servers, relational and in-memory database engines, continuous integration runners, and intermediate data staging or caching tiers that benefit from substantial local scratch space.
